title: Lines of only = or - under a message line render as headings in the timeline export
description:
Found 2026-11-14 during imessage-exporter-djf.9. djf.9 escaped message and balloon lines that read as ATX headings (`# x`), but not setext headings. In Markdown, a line made only of `=` or `-` (0-3 spaces of indentation) directly under a line of text turns that text line into an H1 (`=`) or H2 (`-`). A message such as "Total\n-----" therefore rendered as a heading in the timeline. Tools that split the file on `^#` lines are not affected; Markdown renderers and outline views are.

title: Fix the eleven problems the full code review found in the timeline export, -w and the database hint
description:
Findings from the independent full review of all fork-owned code (2026-11-14, branch worktree-upstream-5-sync at e633c70c, base upstream 47b75148). Every finding was confirmed by running the release binary on synthetic fixtures (under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-review/: chat.db, chat-inline.db, chat-dangling.db, chat-lookup.db, seed.sql) or by reading, as marked. Conductor decisions (taken under Justin's overnight instruction to use the recommended option) are stated per finding.

## Group A — timeline output (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs, timeline_balloons.rs)

F1 (serious, confirmed). One message can turn the rest of timeline.md into a code block. escape_heading_lines escapes only ATX headings. A line that opens a fence (0-3 spaces, then ``` or ~~~) or an HTML block of CommonMark types 1-5 (`<!--`, `<pre`, `<script`, `<style`, `<textarea`, `<?`, `<!` + letter, `<![CDATA[`) passes through; with no closing fence, every later message, day heading and thread heading renders inside it (pandoc CommonMark: 1 h1 instead of 3). Fix: extend the same escape pass (rename it to fit, e.g. escape_block_starts) to put a backslash before a fence opener and before `<` on lines that open HTML block types 1-5. Also fold in djf.11: escape a setext underline (a line of only `=` or only `-`, 0-3 spaces indent, directly under a non-blank text line) so it cannot turn the previous line into a heading — simplest correct shape: backslash before the first `=`/`-` of such a line inside message/balloon text. Handwriting's raw_line fence stays raw. Same call sites as today.

F2 (serious, confirmed). Every reply appears twice, and the nested copy sits under the parent's day showing only a time of day, so a reply sent on Feb 7 reads as sent on Feb 6. Decision: keep both copies, as upstream TXT does, and make each one unambiguous. (a) In the nested (blockquoted) copy, when the reply's local date differs from the parent's date, the header shows the full date and time (e.g. `**Fri, Feb 7, 2025 1:25:24 PM — Me**`). (b) The standalone copy, under its own day, gets one italic line right after its header: `*(reply to a message from <full date and time of the parent>)*`. If the parent cannot be found, use `*(reply to an earlier message)*`.

F3 (confirmed). An attachment is dropped when one text bubble holds several inline stickers or genmoji, and later bubbles can be paired with the wrong attachment: the timeline pairs attachments by position and names at most one per bubble. Fix: use upstream's GUID pairing — iterate `resolve_run(ranges, &mut AttachmentResolver::new(&attachments))` (shared/part.rs) and print one label per attachment range, keeping the sticker/attachment labels from djf.8. Test with upstream's typedstream fixture FormattedInlineStickers.

F7 (confirmed, rare). A message whose date cannot be converted is dropped silently (`Err(_) => return Ok(())` at the date step). Fix: count it in skipped_messages and print a stderr line in the same shape as djf.7's `Skipping message (rowid=…, guid=…): <error>`.

F8 (confirmed by reading). A failed export truncates the previous timeline.md before iteration, leaving a 0-byte file. Fix: write to a temporary file in the same directory and rename it over timeline.md only on success (or open the file only at flush time). A failed run must leave an existing timeline.md byte-identical.

F10 (confirmed by reading). Thread headings reuse Config::filename, which truncates to 235 minus the export path length and replaces characters not allowed in file names, so a long -o path or a group name with `/` or `:` changes the heading. Fix: build the heading from the chat's display name, else the participant names (the same names Config::filename would use, untruncated and unsanitized), else the chat identifier; keep the per-chat cache from djf.5 and its once-per-chat warning behavior. The heading must not depend on the -o path.

## Group B — -w selection, options and the database hint

F4 (confirmed). A -w group whose names all resolve but matches no chat exactly is dropped silently (e.g. `-w alice -w alice,carol` with Carol only in a group that also has Bob exports the Alice DM, exit 0, no warning). Decision: print a stderr warning naming the group (`Warning: --conversation-with group `alice,carol` matched no conversation`), keep exporting the groups that matched; the existing all-groups-empty error stays.

F5 (confirmed on synthetic data). -w selects chat rows, not merged conversations: upstream merges chat rows through chat_lookup (ChatToHandle::dedupe, Config.real_chatrooms), and a sibling row with a different participant set or no participant rows is never selected, so part of a conversation goes missing under the same heading. Fix: after exact matching, also select every chat row whose real_chatrooms id equals a matched row's real_chatrooms id.

F6 (confirmed, damaged DB only). -w drops handles with no handle row (`filter_map(|h| self.real_participants.get(h))`), so a chat {Alice, 77} matches `-w alice` as a DM. Fix: treat an unknown handle as its own distinct participant so the set no longer equals {Alice}.

F9 (confirmed by reading). The database hint (db_access_hint.rs) is missing when the error comes from Options::from_args (the `Invalid command line options` branch in main.rs, reachable through Platform::determine → presence → Inaccessible), and its copy command always names ~/Library/Messages/chat.db even when the failing database is a custom -p path or an iOS backup. Fix: call the hint in that branch too (only for the same error kinds; adapt the classifier if that branch carries a different error type). The copy command must name the database that actually failed: use the path from the error (Inaccessible carries it) or the configured database path; print the ~/Library/Messages form only when the failing path is the default macOS database; for an iOS backup path, omit the copy lines and keep only the Full Disk Access line.

F11 (confirmed by reading). `-c/--copy-method` and `--use-message-times` are accepted with `-f timeline` but do nothing (the timeline never copies attachments or sets file times; an attachments folder may still be created). Decision: print one stderr warning per such option when the format is timeline (`Warning: --copy-method has no effect with --format timeline`), keep going; do not create the attachments folder for timeline if that is reachable in fork-owned code only (otherwise report it).

## Out of scope
- Rendering replies in only one place (rejected in F2's decision).
- Any change to TXT/HTML output or upstream-owned files.

title: Fix the eight problems the second review found in the review fixes (hint copy folder, code fences, nested replies, safe rewrite of timeline.md)
description:
Second independent review (2026-11-14) of the djf.12 fix round (e633c70c..923a5a5b). Synthetic fixtures: /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-review/ (now also chat-replies.db, chat-names.db) and /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-hint/; SQLite WAL experiment /tmp/claude-501/imx-review/walexp/exp.py. Fork-owned code only; `git diff --stat 47b75148 HEAD -- imessage-database` stays empty; txt/, html/, shared/, formatter.rs untouched. Conductor decisions are final.

R1 (serious, confirmed). The hint's copy command reuses /tmp/imx. A second copy (for example an archive chat.db with no -wal) leaves the first database's -wal/-shm in place, and SQLite applies the stale WAL: /tmp/imx/chat.db reads as the FIRST database (50 rows instead of 5 in the experiment). A pre-existing /tmp/imx also keeps another owner's mode or a planted symlink. Decision: copy into a fresh private folder every time. The hint prints, for the default database:
    D=$(mktemp -d /tmp/imx.XXXXXX) && cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db* "$D"/
    imessage-exporter -p "$D"/chat.db <your other options>
and for another database the same with the quoted path and its own file name. Add one line before them: "Run these two lines in the same terminal window." (mktemp -d creates the folder mode 700, so drop `-m 700`.) Update unit tests and the djf.3 description's printed hint text.

R2 (serious, confirmed). F1 escapes every fence opener, including balanced fences closed later in the same text, so code blocks that rendered correctly now render as paragraphs and lose characters (`Vec<String>` -> `Vec`, `a*b*c` -> `abc`). On the real copy all 8 escaped fence lines were 4 closed pairs (pandoc pre 15 -> 11). Decision: track fence state per text: escape an opening fence only when no matching closing fence (same character, at least as long, at most 3 spaces indent, only spaces after) follows within the same text; leave balanced fences and their contents untouched (no escaping inside them at all, including heading/setext/HTML lines inside the fence). HTML types 1-5 stay always-escaped outside fences.

R3 (confirmed). A reply that was later fully unsent is an announcement but is rendered nested as an empty message block (`> **1:25:33 PM — Me**` then `>`). Decision: in the nested loop, render `reply.is_announcement()` through format_announcement, blockquoted.

R4 (confirmed mechanisms). Replies can be nested twice: (a) get_replies returns a reply once per chat_message_join / chat_recoverable_message_join row; (b) a reply to a reply is nested under its parent's own block and again inside the nested copy of that parent. Decision: de-duplicate nested replies by rowid, and nest only one level: the nested copy of a reply does not expand its own replies (they appear nested under that reply's own top-level block). Report the real-copy counts the reviewer suggested (counts only): replies to replies, replies joined to more than one chat (both join tables), empty nested blocks before and after, nested-copy count vs reply-line count after the fix.

R5 (confirmed, also bead djf.15). An unreadable iOS backup root, run without -a iOS, gets a file-copy command for a directory. Decision: when the failing path's kind is unknown, print copy lines only if its file name ends in `.db` and the path is not under `MobileSync/Backup`; otherwise print only the Full Disk Access line. Close djf.15's scope with this.

R6 (confirmed). The .partial rename replaces a symlinked timeline.md with a regular file (the link target keeps stale contents) and resets a 600 file to 644. Decision: if timeline.md exists, resolve it with canonicalize and write the partial file next to the real target; copy the existing file's permissions onto the partial file before the rename.

R7 (plausible). A failing sync_all discards a finished export. Decision: a sync_all error prints a stderr warning and the rename still happens.

R8 (minor, by reading). A parent-lookup error other than not-found skips a readable reply. Decision: fall back to `*(reply to an earlier message)*` and print a stderr warning naming the reply's rowid.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each of R1-R8 has a test that fails before its fix and passes after (negative control shown), except R7 where a unit test with an injected sync error or a clear by-reading argument is acceptable.
2. R1: the printed default-database hint contains `mktemp -d /tmp/imx.XXXXXX`, `"$D"/`, and the same-window line; pasting the printed custom-path pair (with a synthetic source) into zsh copies into a fresh folder and the export command opens that copy. Rerun of the WAL experiment shows the second database's rows.
3. R2: a balanced ``` fence renders as one code block with its contents intact (pandoc CommonMark check if available), an unclosed fence is still escaped, and the fixture-review unclosed-fence case still yields 3 h1 / 6 h2.
4. R3/R4: on chat-replies.db the nested headers equal the reply lines whose parent was found; no empty nested blocks.
5. Real-copy counts (privacy contract of imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2; counts only, exports deleted): exit 0, 1 file; message headers 218239, day headings 3898, thread headings 38282 unchanged; pandoc pre count back to 15 (or explained); nested-copy and reply-line counts before and after, with the gap explained.
6. R6: a 600 timeline.md stays 600 after a rerun; a symlinked timeline.md keeps the link and the target gets the new content.
7. Full gate green: cargo build, cargo test --workspace (0 failures; counts), nightly clippy and fmt, `bun run signal`, `cargo build --release`; `git diff --stat 47b75148 HEAD -- imessage-database` empty.
8. djf.3's description shows the new printed hint; djf.15's notes say R5 resolved it.

title: Show link previews, music, polls and other app messages in the timeline export instead of [App message]
description:
Show app messages (link previews, Apple Music shares, polls, and the other "app balloon" types) in the timeline (Markdown) export, instead of the placeholder `*[App message]*` or the bare message text. Justin picked this as option c on 2026-11-07's work-pick question ("build your own recommended option, and the others too if time allows", relayed 2026-11-14).

## What exists now (commit e2ed95d7, branch worktree-upstream-5-sync; not yet reviewed or merged)
- imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline_balloons.rs (new, fork-owned): `TimelineBalloons` implements upstream's `BalloonFormatter`; `render_app_balloon(config, msg, attachments)` calls upstream's `dispatch_app_balloon`. Registered as `pub(crate) mod timeline_balloons;` in exporters/mod.rs.
- The BubbleComponent::App arm of format_timeline_message (timeline.rs) prints `render_app_balloon(...)`; on Err it prints exactly the pre-djf.2 output via `app_message_fallback` (the message text in italics, or `*[App message]*`). No error type changed.
- Markdown shape: one italic type label line (`*Link*`, `*Music*`, `*Poll*`, `*Apple Pay*`, `*Check In*`, `*Find My*`, `*Location*`, `*App Store*`, `*Collaboration*`, `*Fitness*`, `*Slideshow*`, `*Business*`, `*Handwriting*`, `*Digital Touch*`, or `*<app name>*` for generic apps), then one line per present field, in TXT's template order. URLs are CommonMark autolinks `<scheme:…>` only when they are absolute URIs; anything else (for example a bare `example.com` from the message text) is written as is. Poll options are a Markdown list with vote counts and nested voters (raw handles, as TXT shows them). No escaping layer added.
- Edited messages: a Run part where `is_part_edited` is true gets ` *(edited)*` after its text (or a `*(edited)*` line when the part has no text). No edit-history rendering.
- Run arm: text goes through upstream's `rewrite_fitness_receiver`, as TXT's `body_text_with_translation` does for text bubbles.

## Approach (decided, kept)
- Reuse upstream's decision tree (`dispatch_app_balloon`) and trait; never construct a TXT exporter; never re-parse payloads by hand.
- Fork-owned code only; `git diff --stat 47b75148 HEAD -- imessage-database` empty; no edits to txt/, html/, shared/ or formatter.rs.
- No knob: Justin asked for this and it replaces a placeholder with content (feature-knobs rule: land it on).

## Out of scope
- Rendering attachments' contents, images, or HTML-style cards.
- Any change to the TXT or HTML exporters.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Unit tests in fork-owned code cover at least: URL preview (title + summary + URL), URL with no preview payload (falls back to the URL text), Apple Music, poll with votes and voters, one generic app, and the dispatch-error fallback (`*[App message]*` or the text). Build the test messages the way upstream's txt/tests/balloons.rs does (fixture plists under imessage-database/test_data/).
2. Negative control: with the App arm reverted to the old placeholder code, at least the URL, music and poll tests fail; restored, they pass.
3. Fixture smoke test: `-f timeline` on imessage-database/test_data/db/test.db exits 0; paste the lines of the output that come from app balloons (fixture data, safe to show).
4. Real-copy smoke test on the May database copy (privacy contract of imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2 applies: counts only, never message text): `-f timeline` exits 0 before and after the change, the file count is identical, and `rg -c -F '[App message]'` summed over the output drops (report before and after totals). Delete the export folders afterwards.
5. The edited-message and sticker findings are written into this bead's notes.
6. CARGO_HOME=/tmp/claude-501/cargo-home cargo build, test --workspace (0 failures), clippy --workspace --all-targets (no warnings in fork-owned files), cargo fmt --check, and `bun run signal` all pass.
7. Committed on worktree-upstream-5-sync by explicit path.
notes:
## Status (2026-11-14)
Built, committed (e2ed95d7), not pushed or merged. Awaiting conductor review.

## Verification, per acceptance criterion
- AC1: 30 new tests. timeline_balloons.rs (22, direct BalloonFormatter calls with constructed balloons, like upstream's txt/tests/balloons.rs): every one of the 15 methods, plus business variants, generic-label fallbacks and the autolink rule. timeline.rs (8, end to end through format_timeline_message): URL preview with title and summary (MetadataURL.plist), URL with no preview payload (renders its text as the link), Apple Music (AppleMusic.plist), poll with votes and voters (PollCreate.plist + PollVote.plist + PollVote2.plist as vote rows), generic app (OpenTableInvited.plist), dispatch-error fallback (`*[App message]*`, `*hello*`, URL with neither payload nor text), edited marker, Fitness receiver rewrite. The end-to-end tests seed a copy of test.db (made once per test process under the test temp dir, fixture never written) because payloads are read from the database by rowid.
- AC2 negative controls: App arm set back to the old placeholder code -> exactly 5 tests fail (URL preview, URL without payload, music, poll, generic app), each on its output assertion (left = `*[App message]*` or `*<url text>*`); restored -> pass. Edited marker disabled -> only edited_part_is_marked_edited fails; rewrite_fitness_receiver removed -> only fitness_receiver_placeholder_reads_as_you fails. All restored.
- AC3: `-f timeline` on imessage-database/test_data/db/test.db exits 0, 1 file. The fixture's single-link message (rowid 123445) now renders as `*Link*` / `<https://www.ghacks.net/2020/01/23/lastpass-no-longer-listed-on-the-chrome-web-store/>` / `LastPass no longer listed on the Chrome Web Store - gHacks Tech News` / its summary line; before it was the italic URL only. A seeded scratch copy (/tmp/claude-501/imx-test/fixture-apps/chat.db, seed SQL uses upstream fixture plists) also shows Music, Poll with votes, OpenTable, Apple Pay, the unreadable-app fallback and the edited marker; both binaries exit 0.
- AC4, May real-db copy, counts only, HEAD binary (54485518) vs e2ed95d7: exit 0 both; 1 file both; size 27656 KB -> 28680 KB; `[App message]` 8 -> 0; known type labels 0 -> 8144 (Link 7868, App Store 125, Find My 40, Collaboration 27, Slideshow 24, Business 23, Digital Touch 10, Check In 8, Apple Pay 7, Music 4, Fitness 4, Location 2, Handwriting 2, Poll 0). Generic `*<app name>*` labels cannot be counted without reading names. `*(edited)*` 0 -> 306. Invisible `*U+FFFC*` placeholders 5 -> 0. Unchanged: message headers 218239, reply headers 5846, attachment placeholders 33333, well-formed day headings 3898. Lines starting `# ` 3916 -> 3917 and `## ` 38307 -> 38308: one balloon field each starts with a heading marker (filed as imessage-exporter-djf.9). Exports and logs deleted after counting.
- AC5 findings (seen on the seeded synthetic fixture, timeline vs TXT):
  - Edited message: before djf.2 the timeline showed only the latest text (`Test`) with no sign of the edit; TXT shows the history (`Jan 14, 2025 10:45:56 AM Test` / `Edited 10 seconds later: Test`). Now the timeline shows `Test *(edited)*`. That msg.text holds the latest version is inferred from upstream's body parsing, not checked against a real edited row.
  - Sticker sent as a message: timeline `*[Attachment: outline.heic]*` (nothing says sticker); TXT `Sticker from Me: <path>`, plus the effect or `(App: …)` when metadata exists. Sticker tapback: timeline `- Sticker from <who>` under Tapbacks; TXT adds the file path (code reading; the seeded tapback did not render in either export). Not changed here; filed as imessage-exporter-djf.8.
- AC6: cargo build OK; cargo test --workspace: imessage_database 501, imessage_exporter 649 (619 + 30), doc-tests 42, 0 failures; nightly clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; nightly fmt --check clean; bun run signal 2 pass, 1 not applicable (no TypeScript); cargo build --release OK.
- AC7: committed by explicit path.

## Judgment calls (review these)
- Fields one per line: TXT's connecting words that only name the balloon are dropped, because the italic label names it: `<app> message:` (Fitness, Collaboration, generic), ` transaction:` (Apple Pay), `Photo album:` (Slideshow), the `:` joining Find My's name and status. Fallback texts that stand for a missing value are kept (`unknown amount`, `unknown workout`). Check In's fallback caption `Check In` is dropped, because it only repeats the label.
- Find My shows `*Find My*` then `Find My` (app_name) then the status: strict field parity repeats the name. Same can happen for Fitness. Cosmetic.
- Fields are written one per line with no hard line breaks. Strict CommonMark renderers join consecutive lines into one paragraph; editors that render single newlines as breaks (Obsidian's default) show them on separate lines. Lists (poll, business) render as lists either way.
- Handwriting always renders as ASCII art inside a ``` fence. TXT writes a file when attachment copying is on; the timeline never copies attachments, so it uses TXT's copy-disabled output. The fence is needed because the art is `*` strokes and leading spaces, which Markdown reads as emphasis, lists and code.
- Autolinks only for absolute URIs (CommonMark scheme rule); a bare `example.com` from msg.text stays plain, since `<example.com>` would show literally or parse as an HTML tag.
- Generic app label: app_name, else bundle ID, else `App`. TXT uses app_name even when it is an empty string and then prints no label.
- The fallback is silent: no stderr line per failed balloon (TXT prints the error into the export). Rule 7 check: the fallback output is the old visible text or placeholder, never a neutral value.
- rewrite_fitness_receiver: TXT uses it on text bubbles (body_text_with_translation), not in any balloon method, so it is applied in the timeline's Run arm. This touches text output only when a line starts with the Fitness receiver placeholder.
- TXT's view models (txt/view_model.rs) are pub(super), so the timeline cannot reuse them; it reuses upstream's OptionalText and resolve_check_in_footer and builds lines directly. No upstream visibility widened.

## Follow-ups filed
- imessage-exporter-djf.8: label stickers as stickers in the timeline export.
- imessage-exporter-djf.9: lines starting with `#` in message or balloon text look like day or thread headings (needs an escaping decision).
- imessage-exporter-djf.10: the fallback prints an invisible `*U+FFFC*` when an unreadable app message's text is only the object-replacement character.

title: Make the 'cannot open the Messages database' error say exactly how to fix it on macOS
description:
Make the "can't open the Messages database" error tell the user exactly what to do on macOS. Justin hit this on 2026-05-10: "I don't think the issue is full disk access -- I can access the chat.db file from the terminal." His terminal had Full Disk Access; the exporter still could not open chat.db. Upstream's message (imessage-database/src/error/table.rs, const FULL_DISK_ACCESS) only says to enable Full Disk Access for the terminal emulator, which he had already done.

## Status (2026-11-14): built and verified on worktree-upstream-5-sync in commits f2cf7624 and bceae138 (copy folder mode 700); not pushed, not merged
- New fork-owned file imessage-exporter/src/db_access_hint.rs:
  - db_access_hint(Option<PathBuf>) -> String: the pure hint builder. An empty path counts as None.
  - is_db_access_error(&RuntimeError): true only for DatabaseError(CannotConnect(Permissions(_) | Inaccessible(..))), the two variants upstream ends with its Full Disk Access line.
  - eprint_db_access_hint(&RuntimeError): holds the cfg!(target_os = "macos") gate, calls std::env::current_exe(), prints the hint to stderr.
- imessage-exporter/src/main.rs: one `mod db_access_hint;` line, and one eprint_db_access_hint(&why) call after each of the three error prints ("Invalid configuration" for Config::new, and the two "Unable to export" prints for resolve_filtered_handles and start).
- imessage-database is unchanged: git diff 47b75148 -- imessage-database is empty.

## The hint as printed (after upstream's two lines)
    If your terminal already has Full Disk Access and this still fails, add this program itself in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access:
        <absolute path from current_exe>
    Or copy the database to a folder you can read and point at the copy:
        mkdir -p -m 700 /tmp/imx && cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db* /tmp/imx/
        imessage-exporter -p /tmp/imx/chat.db <your other options>
The copy folder is created mode 700 so other local accounts cannot read the copied message history (conductor decision, 2026-11-14). mkdir sets the mode only when it creates the folder; an existing /tmp/imx keeps its mode.
When current_exe fails or returns an empty path, the first sentence reads "... add this program itself (the imessage-exporter binary you ran) in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access." and no path line is printed. The hint states no cause.

## Out of scope
- Detecting Full Disk Access status programmatically (TCC queries).
- Changing upstream's message text, other error kinds, or Linux/Windows behavior.

## No knob
Message text with no sane "off" state (feature-knobs rule: no switch needed).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Unit tests for the hint builder: with Some(path) the output contains that exact path and both `-p /tmp/imx/chat.db` and the `cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db*` line; with None it contains no empty path and names the binary in words.
2. Smoke test with the release binary on a permission-denied copy of the fixture: copy imessage-database/test_data/db/test.db to a scratch folder under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/, `chmod 000` it, run `-p <that file> -f txt -o <scratch out>`; exit code is non-zero, stderr contains upstream's original message AND the new hint with the binary's absolute path. Paste the stderr (it is fixture-derived, not personal data). Restore permissions and delete the scratch copy afterwards.
3. Negative control: with the hint call removed, the smoke test's stderr lacks the hint; restored, it has it.
4. A normal export of the fixture is unchanged (exit 0, same file count as before the change).
5. CARGO_HOME=/tmp/claude-501/cargo-home cargo build, test --workspace (0 failures), clippy --workspace --all-targets (no warnings in fork-owned files), cargo fmt --check, and `bun run signal` all pass.
6. Committed on worktree-upstream-5-sync by explicit path.
notes:
## Verification evidence (2026-11-14, commits f2cf7624 and bceae138)
- bceae138 (COPY_DB now `mkdir -p -m 700 /tmp/imx && ...`, test constant COPY_LINE updated): cargo test --workspace 501 + 619 + 42 passed, 0 failed; nightly clippy -D warnings and fmt --check clean; bun run signal passes; cargo build --release passes. Smoke test re-run on a fresh chmod 000 fixture copy under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/djf3-700/: exit 1, stderr shows upstream's two lines and the hint with the `mkdir -p -m 700 /tmp/imx` line; scratch copy restored and deleted. The evidence below is from f2cf7624 and still applies except for that one line.
- AC1 unit tests (db_access_hint::tests, 4 tests): with a path, the exact path is on its own line and the cp and -p /tmp/imx/chat.db lines are present; with None, the binary is named in words, no "Full Disk Access:" path intro and no blank line; an empty path gives the same text as None; the classifier is true for Inaccessible and Permissions and false for NotADatabase, QueryError and DiskError.
- AC1 negative control: breaking the path line, the empty-path filter and the Inaccessible arm failed 3 tests on exactly those assertions. Breaking the None branch failed the "names the binary in words" assertion; keeping the words but adding an empty path line failed the "hint has an empty line" assertion. Restored: 4 pass.
- AC2 smoke test: release binary, chmod 000 copy of test.db under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/djf3/, -f txt: exit 1. stderr: upstream's "Invalid configuration: Unable to access `<copy>`: Permission denied (os error 13)" and "Ensure full disk access is enabled for your terminal emulator ..." lines, then the hint with /Users/jhaa/Dev/imessage-exporter/.claude/worktrees/upstream-5-sync/target/release/imessage-exporter. Permissions restored and the scratch folder deleted afterwards.
- AC3 negative control: with the Invalid configuration call removed, the same run exits 1 and prints only upstream's two lines (rg 'add this program itself' finds nothing). Restored: stderr byte-identical to the first run (cmp exit 0).
- AC4: a normal -f txt export of the fixture copy exits 0 with 1 file (orphaned.txt); diff -r against the pre-change baseline export is empty; no hint on stderr. A missing -p file fails earlier, in option validation, and prints no hint.
- AC5: cargo build --workspace passes; cargo test --workspace 501 + 619 + 42 passed, 0 failed (exporter was 615; +4 new); nightly-2026-08-31 clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; nightly fmt --all --check clean; bun run signal passes (LINT and PRETTIER; TS not applicable); cargo build --release passes.

- The hint call also follows the resolve_filtered_handles print (a fork-owned line). That path is not known to produce a connect error; the call is there so every RuntimeError print in main.rs behaves the same.
- The macOS gate is in eprint_db_access_hint, the helper main.rs calls, instead of being repeated at the three main.rs sites. The pure builder has no gate, so its tests run on every platform.
- Builder signature is Option<PathBuf> as scoped.
- Only the Invalid configuration branch was run end to end. The two Unable to export branches use the same helper; they are covered by construction and by the classifier test.

## Resolved points
- Privacy of the copy workaround: resolved in bceae138 by the conductor's decision. The hint now creates the folder with `mkdir -p -m 700 /tmp/imx`, so other local accounts cannot traverse it to read the copy. Residual: mkdir sets the mode only when it creates the folder, so a /tmp/imx that already exists keeps its old mode.
- Cmd+Shift+G tip: declined for now. A cargo install puts the binary under ~/.cargo/bin, a hidden folder that the Full Disk Access "+" file picker reaches with Cmd+Shift+G. The hint does not mention this, because it would add a fact beyond the bead.

title: Timeline export prints the chat-has-no-members warning once per message instead of once per chat
description:
Found during the 5.0.1 sync smoke test (imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2). On the May real-database copy, -f timeline wrote the upstream warning 'Found error: message chat ID N has no members!' 991 times to stderr; -f txt and -f html wrote it once. Cause: chat_display_label in imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs called Config::filename for every collected message, and Config::filename prints that warning each time it runs for a chat with no participants. The txt/html driver memoizes the filename per chat (ExportState.route), so it prints once.

## What exists now (commit bd3707ab, branch worktree-upstream-5-sync; not yet reviewed or merged)
- `ThreadLabels` in timeline.rs: a HashMap<i32, String> of thread headings keyed by the chat rowid that is passed to Config::filename, held by Timeline as `thread_labels`. `thread_key_and_name` (now &mut self) reads the heading from it and computes it with chat_display_label only the first time a chat is seen.
- Keyed by chat rowid, not by the deduplicated real id, so every heading is exactly what an uncached call returns (Config::filename is a pure function of the config and the chat row, apart from the warning).
- A test-only counter (`#[cfg(test)] computed`) counts cache misses for the unit test.
- Config::filename (upstream-owned) is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A unit test in timeline.rs shows chat_display_label/Config::filename runs once per chat across many messages of that chat (e.g. a counter or a cached-label assertion). 2. On the May real-db copy (privacy contract of imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2: counts only), rg -c of 'has no members' in the -f timeline stderr equals the -f txt count (1 on 2026-11-14). 3. The timeline file's day/thread/message header counts are unchanged versus before the fix. 4. cargo build, test --workspace, clippy, fmt check and bun run signal pass.

title: Keep the timeline export going when one message cannot be read, the way the txt and html exports do
description:
Fixed in e836ce82 (awaiting review). In imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs, format_timeline_message uses ? on Attachment::from_message and msg.get_replies, and iter_messages passed that error up, so one unreadable message ended the whole timeline export (exit 1, empty timeline.md). Upstream's shared driver (exporters/shared/driver.rs), used by txt and html, reports such a message and continues. Found by the 2026-11-14 upstream-sync review; the May database copy hits no such error, so this is a robustness fix, not an observed failure.

## Fix (landed)
- iter_messages matches on format_timeline_message. On an error it prints `Skipping message (rowid=<rowid>, guid=<guid>): <error>` on stderr, counts it in the new `skipped_messages` field, leaves the message out and goes on. After the progress bar finishes it prints `<N> messages skipped due to formatting errors.` when N > 0. Both lines are worded exactly as upstream's driver words them.
- Same granularity as upstream: the whole top-level message is skipped, and a reply that cannot be read still skips its parent (TXT's build_replies also propagates with ?).
- Unchanged: a row that cannot be read from the message query itself (`let msg = message?`) still ends the export, as in upstream's driver.
acceptance_criteria: A per-message error in the timeline exporter is reported on stderr with the message id and the export continues; a unit or fixture test forces the error and proves the export still finishes; negative control shown.

title: Lines that start with # in a message or balloon look like day or thread headings in the timeline export
description:
Found 2026-11-14 during imessage-exporter-djf.2; fixed in 50e65059 (awaiting review). The timeline wrote message text and app balloon fields as is, so a line of text that starts with `# ` or `## ` read as a day heading (H1) or a thread heading (H2): Markdown rendered it as a heading, and any reader or tool that splits the file on headings miscounted days and threads.

## Fix (landed, decision option a, narrowed)
- `escape_heading_lines` (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs): a line that CommonMark reads as an ATX heading (0-3 spaces, then 1-6 `#`, then a space, a tab or the end of the line) gets a backslash before its first `#`; Markdown renders it as a plain `#`. Lines end at `\n` or `\r`. Hashtags (`#blessed`), 7+ `#` and lines indented 4+ spaces are left alone. Escaping is idempotent.
- Applied, in fork-owned code only, to: message body text (Run parts and the no-components fallback), the subject, the app fallback text (app_message_fallback), and every balloon line built through `Balloon::line`/`field`/`url` (timeline_balloons.rs). Replies are formatted (and so escaped) before they are blockquoted, so a reply line becomes `> \# …`.
- Not escaped: the handwriting ASCII art inside its ``` fence (new `Balloon::raw_line`; a backslash would show literally in code), the headings the timeline writes itself, announcement lines and tapback lines (they start with `*` or `- `).

## Known gaps left alone (outside the narrowed decision)
- Heading markers after a list marker or a typed blockquote marker (`- # x`, `> # x`): Markdown renders a heading inside the list item or quote. Includes poll option and business item text. They are not day or thread headings for a tool that splits on `^#`.
- Setext headings: a line of only `=` or `-` under a text line renders as an H1/H2 in Markdown. Filed as imessage-exporter-djf.11.

## Decision record
Decision (conductor, 2026-11-14, under Justin's overnight instruction to take the recommended option): option a, narrowed, as above. Option b (document only) was rejected because tools and readers that split the file on headings would still miscount days and threads.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unit tests: '# hi' -> '\# hi'; '## hi' -> '\## hi'; '   # hi' (3 spaces) escaped; '#blessed' unchanged; '####### x' (7 #) unchanged; a heading-shaped line inside a reply's blockquote is escaped. 2. Negative control shown. 3. On the May real-db copy (counts only): lines starting '# ' equal the well-formed day-heading count (3898 on 2026-11-14), and message-header, day and thread-heading counts are otherwise unchanged. 4. Full gate green.

- The subject is escaped too (the decision names body and balloon lines; a subject's later lines are message text the same way).
- `\r` counts as a line ending, as in CommonMark; Messages text can contain a lone `\r`.
- Every `Balloon::line` is escaped, not only `field`: lyrics, Apple Pay and Fitness amounts, poll and business lines. Poll and business lines start with `- `, so their first line never changes; only a later line of a multi-line value can.
